name: dotnet-xunit

Author xUnit v3 tests for .NET 8.0+, covering `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`, data sources, `IClassFixture`, `ICollectionFixture`, `IAsyncLifetime`, parallelism, assertions, output, analyzers, and v2 migration.

Prerequisites: Test project already scaffolded via [skill:dotnet-add-testing] with xUnit packages referenced. Run [skill:dotnet-version-detection] to confirm .NET 8.0+ baseline for xUnit v3 support. See [skill:dotnet-testing-strategy], [skill:dotnet-integration-testing], [skill:dotnet-snapshot-testing].

v3 uses `xunit.v3`, `xunit.runner.visualstudio` (3.x), `ValueTask`, `xunit.v3.assert` or `xunit.v3.assert.source`, and strongly typed `TheoryDataRow<T>`. v2 uses `xunit`, `Task`, and `IEnumerable<object[]>`. v3 removes assertion message parameters; use custom assertions or `Assert.Fail()`. Migration mainly changes `IAsyncLifetime`, `[ClassData]`, and assertion messages.

Use `[Fact]` for parameterless tests; `[Theory]` for varying inputs. Prefer `[InlineData]` for simple, nearby data; use `[MemberData]`/`[ClassData]` for complex/shared data. **One fact per `[Fact]`, one concept per `[Theory]`.** If a `[Theory]` tests fundamentally different scenarios, split into separate `[Fact]` methods.

Fixtures: **Use `IClassFixture` for expensive shared resources** within one class; **Use `ICollectionFixture` when multiple classes share the same resource.** **Use `IAsyncLifetime` for async setup/teardown** instead of constructors and `IDisposable`; v3 returns `ValueTask`, v2 `Task`.

Classes in a collection run sequentially; different collections run in parallel. Unattributed classes are separate implicit collections. Use:
`[CollectionDefinition("Sequential", DisableParallelization = true)]`
**Do not disable parallelism globally.** Instead, group tests that share mutable state into named collections.

Create `xunit.runner.json` in the test project root:
`"$schema": "https://xunit.net/schema/current/xunit.runner.schema.json",`
Ensure it is copied to output:
`<Content Include="xunit.runner.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />`

Use `ITestOutputHelper` for per-test diagnostics; bridge via `ILoggerProvider` when needed. **Do not use constructor-injected `ITestOutputHelper` in static methods.** Store it in an instance field, not a static one.

Create domain-specific assertions. `Assert.Multiple` is available in v3; v2 requires separate assertions.

Enable xUnit analyzers in all test projects. In `.editorconfig`:
`dotnet_diagnostic.xUnit1004.severity = suggestion`
Important rules: xUnit1004, xUnit1012, xUnit

name: dotnet-xunit

Author xUnit v3 tests for .NET 8.0+, covering `[Fact]`, `[Theory]`, data sources, `IClassFixture`, `ICollectionFixture`, `IAsyncLifetime`, parallelism, assertions, output, analyzers, and v2 migration.

Prerequisites: Test project already scaffolded via [skill:dotnet-add-testing] with xUnit packages referenced. Run [skill:dotnet-version-detection] to confirm .NET 8.0+ baseline for xUnit v3 support. See [skill:dotnet-testing-strategy], [skill:dotnet-integration-testing], [skill:dotnet-snapshot-testing].

v3 uses `xunit.v3`, `xunit.runner.visualstudio` (3.x), `ValueTask`, `xunit.v3.assert` or `xunit.v3.assert.source`, and strongly typed `TheoryDataRow<T>`. v2 uses `xunit`, `Task`, and `IEnumerable<object[]>`. v3 removes assertion message parameters; use custom assertions or `Assert.Fail()`. Migration mainly changes `IAsyncLifetime`, `[ClassData]`, and assertion messages.

Use `[Fact]` for parameterless tests; `[Theory]` for varying inputs. Prefer `[InlineData]` for simple, nearby data; use `[MemberData]`/`[ClassData]` for complex/shared data. **One fact per `[Fact]`, one concept per `[Theory]`.** If a `[Theory]` tests fundamentally different scenarios, split into separate `[Fact]` methods.

Fixtures: **Use `IClassFixture` for expensive shared resources** within one class; **Use `ICollectionFixture` when multiple classes share the same resource.** **Use `IAsyncLifetime` for async setup/teardown** instead of constructors and `IDisposable`; v3 returns `ValueTask`, v2 `Task`.

Classes in a collection run sequentially; different collections run in parallel. Unattributed classes are separate implicit collections. Use:
`[CollectionDefinition("Sequential", DisableParallelization = true)]`
**Do not disable parallelism globally.** Instead, group tests that share mutable state into named collections.

Create `xunit.runner.json` in the test project root:
`"$schema": "https://xunit.net/schema/current/xunit.runner.schema.json",`
Ensure it is copied to output:
`<Content Include="xunit.runner.json" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />`

Use `ITestOutputHelper` for per-test diagnostics; bridge via `ILoggerProvider` when needed. **Do not use constructor-injected `ITestOutputHelper` in static methods.** Store it in an instance field, not a static one.

Create domain-specific assertions. `Assert.Multiple` is available in v3; v2 requires separate assertions.

Enable xUnit analyzers in all test projects. In `.editorconfig`:
`dotnet_diagnostic.xUnit1004.severity = suggestion`
Important rules: xUnit1004, xUnit1012, xUnit1025, xUnit2000, xUnit2002, xUnit2007, xUnit2013, xUnit2017.

**Do not forget to make fixture classes `public`.** xUnit requires fixture types to be public with a public parameterless constructor (or `IAsyncLifetime`). Non-public fixtures cause silent failures.
**Do not mix `[Fact]` and `[Theory]` on the same method.** A method is either a fact or a theory, not both.
**Do not return `void` from async test methods.** Return `Task` or `ValueTask`. `async void` tests report false success because xUnit cannot observe the async completion.
**Do not use `[Collection]` without a matching `[CollectionDefinition]`.** An unmatched collection name silently creates an implicit collection with default behavior.

References: https://xunit.net/; https://xunit.net/docs/getting-started/v3/migration; https://xunit.net/xunit.analyzers/rules/; https://xunit.net/docs/shared-context; https://xunit.net/docs/configuration-files
